title: POC Rapid Scaling & Cost Simulation — Dedicated GPU Pools
content:
Summary:

Quick exploratory POC notes and runbook for sizing dedicated GPU capacity, tuning autoscaling policy, and producing conservative GPU cost estimates. This doc is intentionally concise and experiment-driven — to be used in the 2-week customer POC for MonetaAI (private deployment evaluation).

Objectives:
- Validate target latency SLOs at target concurrency for the chat completion use case.
- Produce three capacity scenarios (conservative / recommended / aggressive) with hourly cost and per-million-token cost estimates.
- Deliver an autoscaling policy that balances latency SLOs and cost (minimize idle GPUs while preventing queue growth).
- Provide an experimental checklist and run steps to measure real token throughput and KV cache hit effects.

Customer constraints and acceptance criteria (from kickoff):
- 99th percentile response latency <= 200ms at steady-state 200 QPS (user-facing chat routing).
- Typical generation length: 120 tokens avg (sampling), prompt avg 80 tokens -> total tokens per call ~200
- SLA: 99.9% availability, graceful fallback to smaller model within 300ms on overload
- Security: Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed KMS, no external model calls.

Assumptions used for quick calc (explicit so we can iterate):
- Model: open-llm family "redwood-13b-light" (decoder-only, KV cache enabled)
- Serving latency per token on GPU (p50/p95 per-step): p50 = 0.8ms, p95 = 2.5ms for H100 80GB-like perf (batching=auto, quantized int8 path).
- Average effective batch size in practice: 16 tokens-per-batch across concurrent requests (due to prefix diversity)
- KV cache hit rate for chat sessions: 45% after warmup (saves ~35% of autoregressive steps).
- GPU options considered: A100-40GB, H100-80GB, L4-48GB (inference-optimized) — list hourly rates are indicative and will be validated with finance: A100: $3.20/hr, H100: $6.50/hr, L4: $1.75/hr.

Back-of-envelope throughput model (single GPU):
- Tokens/sec_per_gpu = (1 / per-token-latency_ms) * 1000 * effective_batching_factor
- Using p95 per-token = 2.5ms -> single GPU tokens/sec = (1/2.5)*1000 * 16 = 6.4k tokens/sec -> 384k tokens/min -> 23M tokens/hr
- Requests per second (RPS) supported = tokens/sec_per_gpu / avg_tokens_per_request -> 6400 / 200 = 32 RPS per GPU (p95 target)
- For target steady 200 RPS at p95, GPUs_needed = ceil(200 / 32) = 7 GPUs -> round to 8 for headroom and maintenance.

Scenario table (conservative / recommended / aggressive):
- Conservative (SLO cushion, prefer lower variance): min=6 GPUs, target=10 GPUs, max=14 GPUs; GPU type: H100; hourly cost (target 10 * 6.5) = $65/hr.
- Recommended (balanced): min=4 GPUs, target=8 GPUs, max=12 GPUs; GPU type: A100; hourly cost (target 8 * 3.2) = $25.6/hr.
- Aggressive (cost-optimized with more batching and quantization): min=3 GPUs, target=6 GPUs, max=10 GPUs; GPU type: L4; hourly cost (target 6 * 1.75) = $10.5/hr.

Per-million-token cost estimates (rough):
- Compute cost per token = (GPU hourly rate) / (tokens_per_hour_per_gpu)
- Using tokens_per_hour_per_gpu = 23,000,000 tokens/hr (from above) ->
  - H100: $6.50 / 23M = $0.000283/token -> $283 per million tokens
  - A100: $3.20 / 23M = $0.000139/token -> $139 per million tokens
  - L4: $1.75 / 23M = $0.000076/token -> $76 per million tokens
- Add network, infra overhead, and reserved-capacity amortization -> apply multiplier 1.25x to capture infra/service overhead and inefficiencies.
  - H100 end-to-end: ~$354 /M tokens; A100: ~$174 /M tokens; L4: ~$95 /M tokens (ballpark).

Notes on validity: these numbers assume sustained throughput with steady batching and do not capture request preemption, cold-starts, or autoscale lag. Real measured throughput can be 15-30% lower for elastic multi-tenant pools depending on interference.

Autoscaling policy recommendation (starter):
- Metrics used: queued_requests, p95_latency, GPU_utilization, outstanding_tokens (sum of tokens across queued requests).
- Scale-up triggers (fast path):
  - queued_requests > 30 for 30s OR
  - p95_latency > target_p95 (200ms) for 15s AND GPU_utilization > 60%
  - outstanding_tokens / tokens_per_gpu_estimate > 1.2 (i.e., projected overload)
- Scale-down triggers (conservative):
  - queued_requests == 0 AND GPU_utilization < 30% for 5 minutes AND p95_latency <= target_p95
  - cooldown window after any scale-down: 10 minutes (to avoid flapping)
- Scale step sizes: add 1 GPU on scale-up events up to step limit 3 GPUs (if multiple triggers persist, apply again after 30s). Scale-down size: remove 1 GPU at a time.
- Pre-warm policy for predictable daily peaks: schedule pre-warm to target pool size 10 minutes before known peak windows using traffic forecasting (can use lightweight linear model from last 7 days).
- Fallbacks: route overflow to hosted-tier model (cheaper, lower-capacity) or lower-accuracy quantized variant; this should be automatic within 300ms if scale-up can't catch up.

Operational runbook (POC experiments):
1) Baseline measurement (no autoscale): deploy single model replica on 1 GPU, run synthetic load increasing RPS in 10 RPS steps up to 240 RPS. Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and batch size distribution.
2) KV cache warmup: simulate persistent chat sessions; measure cache hit rate after 5/10/20 request sequences; record latency delta and token savings.
3) Multi-GPU pool test: deploy pool sizes [4,6,8,10] and repeat workload. Capture scaling efficiency = observed RPS per GPU relative to single-GPU baseline.
4) Autoscale tuning: enable autoscaler with tuned thresholds, run a burst test (baseline 50 RPS, spike to 300 RPS for 90s) and observe scale-up time and p95 latency.
5) Cost replay: using measured tokens/hr per GPU compute actual $/M tokens for each GPU type and scenario.

Quick checklist for POC day 0 (prep):
- Confirm model binary fits GPU memory with quantization plan (int8 vs fp16) and KV cache margins.
- Confirm networking egress limits (private deployment) and that per-node NIC bandwidth >= 25Gbps for H100 pools.
- Provision three node types for experiment (A100, H100, L4) with identical infra for fair comparison.
- Setup Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard with endpoints: queued_requests, tokens_in_flight, avg_batch_size, p50/p95_latency, gpu_utilization, pool_size, eviction_counts.
- Create Jupyter notebook to calculate cost-per-token from measured metrics (persist as artifact).

Open questions & risks (to address in workshop):
- Exact per-hour pricing is unknown until capacity contract negotiated (finance to confirm). Current rates are placeholders and will change impactfully on $/M results.
- Model architecture differences (13B vs 70B) will materially change token latency — ensure we test on the target model variant.
- Multi-tenant interference: if we run shared pools for POC, need isolation tests to measure noise; dedicated single-tenant pools preferred for accurate perf numbers.

Deliverables by end of POC (2 weeks):
- Measured throughput curves (RPS vs p95 latency) for each GPU type and pool size (CSV + plots).
- Recommended autoscaling policy (YAML for scheduler) and suggested min/target/max pool sizes per customer SLO.
- Cost sheet: $/hour and $/million-token for three scenarios, sensitivity analysis +-20% throughput.
- Short exec summary (1 page) with recommended procurement path (Dedicated vs Mixed Reserved + Burst).

Appendix: quick math snippets (copyable)
- tokens_per_gpu = (1000 / p95_token_ms) * effective_batch_size
- rps_per_gpu = tokens_per_gpu / avg_tokens_per_request
- gpus_required = ceil(target_rps / rps_per_gpu)

Next immediate steps:
- Run baseline single-GPU perf tests for model binary (assigned to Liam).
- Finance to confirm indicative GPU rates (Priya).
- Schedule 2-hour workshop with MonetaAI to review acceptance criteria and peak patterns (Marcus to schedule).

Notes to self (informal):
- If KV cache hit >60%, tokens/hr per GPU jumps by ~30% — big lever for capacity savings.
- Watch out for tail latency from long prompts; consider request-level preemption to keep p95 low.
- Keep the POC focused: measure what changes cost estimate materially and don't over-index on tiny micro-optimizations.

End of doc.
